name: Knowledge Graph-based Learning Path Recommendation
venue: Knowledge-Based Systems; Information Processing & Management; AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence; Electronics survey
problem_setting: Generate personalized learning paths rather than isolated resource rankings by using educational knowledge graphs that encode concepts, resources, prerequisite relations, hierarchy, similarity, difficulty, learner mastery, and learning goals. The task is to choose an ordered sequence of concepts or exercises that is pedagogically feasible, aligned with the learner's current state and target concept, and explainable through graph paths or relation constraints.
core_method: Representative methods construct a multidimensional educational knowledge graph over learning objects, concepts, courses, exercises, and learner interactions, then generate and rank candidate paths under prerequisite, semantic similarity, difficulty, and learner-preference constraints. The 2020 multidimensional KG model stores learning objects in categories such as Basic Knowledge, Algorithms, and Tasks, defines multiple semantic relations, generates candidate paths with reverse-greedy graph search, and ranks paths according to structural constraints and learner needs. Later work adds local and global context from learner postings, GCN or ant-colony optimization over concept-resource layers, and learner mastery estimation. The latest representative KnowLP method uses EDU-GraphRAG to generate prerequisite and similarity knowledge-structure graphs from concept names and explanations, then applies a Discrimination Learning-driven Reinforcement Learning module with prerequisite, similarity, and difficulty agents so that similarity relations can act as a fallback when prerequisite-only paths cause blocked learning.
data_sources: Common data sources include manually or semi-automatically constructed educational knowledge graphs, course concept taxonomies, learning-object metadata, textbooks or course materials, MOOC behavior logs, learner-resource interactions, exercise records, and public educational datasets. KnowLP reports Junyi from PSLC DataShop, MOOCCubeX, and ASSISTments2009, with 835, 443, and 167 knowledge concepts respectively; Junyi has an explicit prerequisite graph, MOOCCubeX has an incomplete graph, and ASSISTments2009 lacks a knowledge-structure graph. Broader KG-LPR studies may use domain-specific course graphs, online learning community postings, MOOCCube-style datasets, or teacher-curated prerequisite maps. [uncertain]
evaluation_metrics: Typical evaluation includes normalized mastery improvement or learning gain after a recommended path, performance at fixed path lengths such as 5, 10, 15, and 20 steps, prerequisite consistency, path coherence, difficulty smoothness, learner satisfaction or expert review, path explanation quality, runtime, and ablation effects. Some papers also report Precision, Recall, NDCG, Hit@K, semantic similarity, learning time, or path cost, but there is no single standardized metric suite across the field. KnowLP uses comparative performance tables, statistical significance testing against DLPR, similarity-agent ablation, generated-graph analysis, simulation experiments, runtime analysis, and threshold sensitivity. [uncertain]
baselines: Representative baselines include prerequisite-only graph search, shortest path or A* search, reverse-greedy path generation, collaborative filtering, KNN, matrix factorization, content-based recommendation, GRU4Rec, Actor-Critic, RL-Tutor, CSEAL, SRC, GEHRL, DLPR, graph convolutional recommendation, ant colony optimization, genetic algorithm variants, and ablations that remove similarity, difficulty, learner-state, or generated-graph components. Exact baseline sets vary substantially by paper and dataset. [uncertain]
strengths: The approach provides strong pedagogical interpretability because each recommendation can be traced to prerequisite, hierarchy, similarity, difficulty, or learner-state relations. It fits domains where teachers already maintain concept maps, syllabi, or learning-object metadata, and it can combine curriculum structure with learner mastery rather than relying only on clicks. It supports multi-objective optimization, including mastery gap reduction, prerequisite readiness, difficulty progression, learning cost, and target relevance. Recent dual-graph methods improve robustness by avoiding blocked learning when strict prerequisite chains are incomplete or ineffective.
limitations: Effectiveness depends on knowledge graph coverage, relation correctness, exercise-concept tagging, and learner-state estimation quality. High-quality educational KGs are expensive to build and maintain, and automatically generated prerequisite or similarity edges require verification to avoid pedagogically wrong paths. Cross-paper comparison is difficult because datasets, path definitions, candidate spaces, and metrics are inconsistent. Many evaluations are offline or simulation-based, so real learning gain, long-term retention, and teacher acceptance remain under-tested. Full RL or GraphRAG-enhanced variants also introduce higher computational cost and operational complexity.
fit_for_current_project: High fit. The current course recommendation agent already includes a Go backend, Vue frontend, Neo4j knowledge graph, recommendation modules, learning-progress data, and DeepSeek integration. The method can be transferred by representing AI-course concepts, resources, exercises, prerequisites, similarity links, and difficulty annotations in Neo4j, estimating learner mastery from progress and question records, and generating explainable next-step or full-path recommendations. A pragmatic project version should start with prerequisite-constrained path generation and mastery-gap ranking, then add similarity fallback, difficulty smoothing, and LLM-assisted edge completion after graph quality checks.
implementation_complexity: Medium to high. A minimal version is feasible with Neo4j schemas, Cypher traversal, topological or shortest-path search, and rule-based ranking over mastery gap, prerequisite readiness, resource quality, and difficulty. A research-grade version requires robust KG construction, teacher review workflows, learner mastery modeling, graph completion, multi-objective ranking, offline evaluation, ablation baselines, and possibly GNN, reinforcement learning, or GraphRAG components. [uncertain]
paper_patent_value: High. For a CCF-B-oriented paper, the strongest contribution would be an explainable adaptive KG learning-path framework that combines verified prerequisite constraints, similarity fallback for blocked learning, learner mastery estimation, difficulty-aware exercise selection, and reproducible ablations on path quality and learning gain. For patent claims, valuable points include dual prerequisite-similarity educational graph construction, blocked-learning detection, dynamic strategy switching among prerequisite, similarity, and difficulty decisions, and graph-grounded explanations for recommended learning paths.
recommended_action: Implement a staged prototype: first standardize concept, resource, exercise, prerequisite, similarity, and difficulty schemas in Neo4j for the AI curriculum; second compute learner mastery from quizzes, progress, and question records; third generate prerequisite-valid candidate paths with Cypher and rank them by mastery gap, prerequisite readiness, difficulty smoothness, resource quality, and target relevance; fourth add similarity fallback when prerequisite paths are blocked or low-confidence; fifth add DeepSeek-assisted edge suggestions with teacher review and provenance; sixth evaluate against shortest-path, prerequisite-only, KNN or collaborative filtering, and ablated scoring baselines using offline metrics plus teacher-reviewed path quality.
